also: take things out of the bag

terms.grammar: solvō, solvere, solvī, solūtum with sarcinās as object
evidence: Front. Strat. 1.5.3: praecēpit suīs, nē sarcinās solverent aut onera dēpōnerent
terms.comment: Frontinus’s phrase for soldiers told not to unpack their kit, so that the enemy would think they were staying: the opposite of sarcinās colligere, to pack. To take a thing out of a bag, dēprōmere (Cicero: pecūniam ex arcā dēprōmere); to put the bags down on arriving, sarcinās dēpōnere. See the examples.

phrases.english: Put the bags down; we’ll unpack them later.

phrases.latin: Age, sarcinās solvāmus et vestēs in armārium repōnāmus.
phrases.english: Come on, let’s unpack and put the clothes away in the wardrobe.
Take your toys out of the bags.

phrases.latin: praecēpit suīs, nē sarcinās solverent aut onera dēpōnerent
phrases.english: he told his men not to unpack their kit or put down their loads

sources: Lewis & Short: solvo · Lewis & Short: sarcina · Lewis & Short: depromo
